title: Strict local curve reduction and costalk identifications
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Noetherian means having a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and excellent means having an affine cover by spectra of excellent rings. On small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], for a closed immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow V$ with complementary open $b$, write $a^!$ for the right derived functor of $a^{-1}\ker(1\to b_*b^{-1})$ on $\Lambda$-module sheaves [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a point $z$ and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, put $C_z(K)=i_z^!(K|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}})$, where $i_z:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}$ is the closed point [def-weil-residue-field]. For a geometric point $\bar z$ above $z$, let $C_{\bar z}(K)$ be its geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-point]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$C_{\bar z}(K)\simeq R\Gamma_{\{z_0\}}(X_{(\bar z)},K|_{X_{(\bar z)}}),$$
where $X_{(\bar z)}$ is the strict localization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], $z_0$ its closed point, and supported cohomology is [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections].

Suppose $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ is a geometric specialization, meaning an $X$-map $X_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$, and is immediate, meaning that the reduced closure $Z$ of the image of $\bar y$ in $X_{(\bar x)}$ has Krull dimension $1$ (the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets). Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X_{(\bar x)}$ and $L=i^!(K|_{X_{(\bar x)}})$. Then $Z$ is an integral excellent strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Its normalization $\nu:\widetilde Z\to Z$ in its function field [def-sc-normalization] is finite and a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]; $\widetilde Z$ is the spectrum of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The generic point is unchanged. If $z_0$ and $\widetilde z_0$ are the closed points, then $\kappa(\widetilde z_0)/\kappa(z_0)$ is finite purely inseparable, of degree a power of the residue characteristic (degree $1$ in characteristic zero), hence its degree is invertible in $\Lambda$.

Inverse image along $\nu$ is an equivalence of etale sheaf categories. With the geometric points induced by the specialization and its unique lift to $\widetilde Z$, there are natural isomorphisms
$$C_{\bar y}(K)\simeq C_{\bar y}(L)\simeq(\nu^*L)_{\bar\eta},\qquad C_{\bar x}(K)\simeq C_{\bar x}(L)\simeq R\Gamma_{\{\widetilde z_0\}}(\widetilde Z,\nu^*L).$$
On the middle terms $C$ is computed on $Z$. These isomorphisms respect the Tate twists defined by roots of unity and the cohomological shifts.
